title: Redirector hosts, unwrappable links and special-case rules
description: Rules that go beyond plain host matching: URL unwrapping for redirector links, and hosts that must never be containerized even though they match a Google pattern.
notesRedirectors: When a *containerized* tab navigates through one of these redirectors to a non-Google destination, the destination is resolved from the listed query parameter and opened OUTSIDE the container. Params are read in order; the first absolute http(s) URL wins.
notesNeverContainerize: Host+path prefixes for federated-sign-in widgets that are embedded by third parties. These are only ever loaded as sub-resources or popups belonging to another site, so containerizing them breaks 'Sign in with Google' on non-Google sites. Matching is prefix based on host + pathname.
notesOauthPaths: Paths on accounts.google.com that form part of a third-party OAuth flow. When such a navigation is started by a non-Google opener and 'oauthPassthrough' is enabled, the flow runs inside the Google container (so the Google session is reused) and the callback is released back to the relying party's own cookie jar.
